summary: xAI announced that it is open-sourcing Grok Build, its coding agent and terminal UI harness, making the agent loop, tools, terminal UI, and extension system available on GitHub, including the ability to run it against local inference.

mechanisms.reason: The harness can now be pointed at local inference instead of a hosted API, moving some inference workload off datacentre infrastructure for developers who choose this path.
mechanisms.quote: Finally, Grok Build can now run fully local-first: compile it yourself, point it at your own local inference, and drive everything from your config.toml .

practices.reason: The open-sourced agent loop, tool dispatch, and extension system (skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, subagents) is now readable and implementable code that an engineering team could study or fork to build their own agent scaffolding.
practices.quote: The agent loop: how context is assembled, how model responses are parsed, and how tool calls are dispatched

practices.reason: Teams could self-host the harness against their own inference backend, which changes what needs to be integrated and configured versus using the hosted product.
practices.quote: compile it yourself, point it at your own local inference, and drive everything from your config.toml
